title: Edge telemetry conduit: tenant-segregated pipeline for Dedicated & Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated and Private deployments currently route telemetry (metrics, logs, traces) through a shared ingress which increases risk of noisy neighbors, makes per-tenant rate-limiting hard, and complicates on-prem upgrade windows. We need a tenant-segregated observability conduit that enforces isolation at the edge, preserves tracing context, and supports offline/on-prem buffering without changing the runtime API surface.

Goals: 
- Provide per-tenant logical isolation for telemetry with clear quotas and enforcement.
- Maintain end-to-end tracing: propagate trace/span IDs from runtime through edge and into backend ingestion.
- Offer a resilient on-prem buffer mode that tolerates backend outages and backpressure.
- Minimize perf overhead at the runtime path (target added latency <1ms per request on p99).
- Integrate with existing OTLP/Prometheus stacks and Redwood Console dashboards.

Non-goals: cross-tenant aggregation for hosted analytics (handled in separate pipeline), deep log parsing at edge (keep edge lightweight).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Telemetry edge component accepts OTLP/HTTP requests with tenant header and writes to tenant-scoped queue.
2) Traces retain original trace_id and span_id when viewed in Console for Dedicated customers.
3) Under a simulated backend outage, edge buffers up to configured retention and resumes flush without data loss.
4) No regression >1ms p99 added latency in local perf tests.
5) Unit and integration tests covering tenant tagging, TLS/mTLS auth, and circuit-breaking behavior.
updates: 2025-02-18 - Aisha: Kickoff — collected examples of failure modes from support logs. Linked design doc. Decided to avoid per-tenant dedicated collectors in hardware; prefer logical isolation at edge to reduce ops burden.

2025-02-24 - Liam: Prototype of edge conduit completed (in branch feat/edge-conduit). Implements tenant header extraction, basic queueing, and OTLP passthrough. Local perf looks promising (p50 +0.25ms).

2025-03-01 - Design review: PM and Security feedback documented. Decided on mTLS between edge and backend for on-prem, and optional API-key for legacy agents. Security asked for HMAC verification on tenant header when across untrusted networks.

2025-03-03 - Eng update: Added per-tenant circuit breaker and token bucket rate limiter. Experiment shows isolation prevents noisy-tenant queue build-up. Filing follow-up to tune defaults. Linked PR #6789 and load test results.

2025-03-04 - QA: Integration tests for trace propagation failing in 2/10 runs due to header rewrite in legacy reverse proxy. Action: add passthrough config and update docs for customers running proxies.
implementation_notes: Edge component will run as a small Go service (single binary) deployed in customer VPC/on-prem as a daemonset or VM. Use OpenTelemetry Collector SDK for receiver/processor/exporter plumbing.
Tenant identification: prefer X-Redwood-Tenant header injected by runtime. Fall back to mTLS SAN mapping when header missing.
Queueing: use per-tenant persistent ring buffer on disk with configurable size (default 1GB) and backpressure via TCP reset to runtime when full.
Security: require mTLS for on-prem to backend. Support envelope encryption using KMS when configured. HMAC signature verification on tenant header for cross-network deployments.
Tracing: preserve trace_id/span_id in OTLP payload. Add edge.local_span as a child span to capture edge processing time without overwriting customer spans.
Metrics: emit edge_internal.* metrics (ingest.latency, buffer.size, drop.count) tagged by tenant for Console dashboards and alerting.
Config: expose rate_limit_per_minute, buffer_size_bytes, otlp_endpoint, mTLS_cert_paths, hmac_secret_ref as top-level flags.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for header extraction, HMAC verification, and queueing.
- Integration tests: runtime -> edge -> backend with trace verification.
- Fault injection: network partitions, backend delays, sudden tenant traffic spikes.
- Load test: 10k req/s sustained across 200 tenants to validate isolation and latency SLOs.
rollout_plan:
1) Canary in internal staging with 2 tenants; 24h smoke and load observation.
2) Invite 5 pilot customers on Dedicated; run for 2 weeks and collect telemetry.
3) Gradual ramp to all Dedicated clusters with feature flag.
4) Offer automated migration guide for Private customers; require manual opt-in for on-prem installs.
5) Post-rollout audit and SLO review after 30 days.
